purpose: Bound enrollment response allocation and the complete discovery/claim-or-reconnect operation without changing presentation or server protocol.
previousTurn: progress: C82 was implemented, verified, committed and pushed

repositoryInventory.otherRepositories: No modifications made; existing Runtime and developer-portal work preserved.
repositoryInventory.activeIntake: TinyRustLM Content and Improvement contain only placeholders.

findings: Content-Length could reject a known oversized body, but absent or misleading headers reached arrayBuffer before the one-MiB check.
Fetch and body reads had no deadline or caller cancellation.
An in-flight shared contract promise could couple independent callers when cancellation was added.
Existing UI generates a new claim idempotency key on each click; client recovery alone does not solve that separate behavior.

observations: Oversized response consumed whole-body API and reported invalid_response after allocation.
A delayed Fetch completed despite a requested short deadline.
Discovery and claim exceeded the operation budget without failure.

implementation.budgetScope: One caller operation across contract discovery and its dependent claim or reconnect, including every body read.
implementation.signal: Optional options.signal on discover, request, claim and reconnect; validated before work. Fetch receives the derived signal.
implementation.body: Require ReadableStream; reject declared oversize, bound each decoded chunk before copying, preserve split UTF-8, cancel failures and release readers. No arrayBuffer/text fallback.
implementation.lateCompletion: Abort Fetch on terminal failure and discard late returned bodies. Cancellation promises are observed without extending the deadline.
implementation.cache: Cache only a successfully validated contract; concurrent discovery operations have independent lifetimes.
implementation.mutation: No automatic POST retry. An explicit client call with the same idempotency key preserves its identity for recovery; server persistence can remain unknown after timeout.
implementation.shells: Move the existing lifetime script before enrollment in the canonical shell and regenerate both current asset-hashed shells.
implementation.unchanged: No model, schema, styling, visible copy, dependency or NuGet package version change.

realFetchObservations: Loopback server observes timeout/cancel response closure.
browser.continuity: Existing desktop-only two-profile explicit-save/restore/replay/credential-nonpersistence case passes against the loopback service. Three other-project skips remain declared.
browser.boundary: Local test services and synthetic inference only. No real account or live service operation.

visual.boundary: Exact empty-state desktop/mobile screenshot bytes and recorded fields match, without masks. This does not remove the older C63/C82 historical-baseline differences.

limits: Abort does not undo an already persisted server mutation.
The UI must still retain a pending claim identity for same-key user retry. No such UI recovery is claimed by these client tests.
Separate memory submit/search/outbox calls retain their existing request lifetime limitations.
A dependency that ignores cancellation may keep running, but its late result is not admitted.
No real model, live seed, live memory, Linux ARM64 package proof, NuGet push or deployment.
Known policy-blocked deletions and source-admission limitations remain; none were retried.

secretScan.boundary: Checkpoint files only; scan preceded final scan/cleanup accounting fields. No NuGet key contents read.

ownedOutput.method: Confirmed no matching live writers, verified original ownership, inventoried exact bounded output, removed through the shared ownership helper and verified absence.
